headline: Global Microsoft Alliance Marketing Leader | Associate Director at EY
about:
As a global marketing executive and energized change agent, I bring technologies to life. I work at the intersection of creative expression and customer-centricity—balancing innovation and strategy with pragmatic sales execution to drive market-leading growth.

My experience spearheading holistic multi-channel marketing (traditional, digital, social)—at Fortune 300, startup, and high-growth companies—centers on cross-industry value-creation in high-tech, retail, CPG, professional services, and other industries.

Over the years, I pioneered and expanded customer-centric integrated marketing and communications—through digital thought leadership, social media, market research, product marketing and customer insights—and delivered transformational GTM solutions and content that broke the mold for clients in industry sectors.

I currently lead Big Play global marketing campaigns, including cloud-based intelligent platforms that represent the MAAGs at Accenture. Through precision marketing, I created marketplace cohesion, strengthened business alignment, and positioned the firm as the #1 global systems integrator with Salesforce and Workday.

Collaborating with senior leadership, I advanced Accenture's thought leadership in various areas—most notably in shaping the "Leading Through Change" webcast with Accenture/Salesforce CEOs. The online event engaged 9.9+ million live viewers and was lauded as a highly innovative and empathetic response to COVID.  

Another highlight from my diverse career is from my time at HPE/EDS as Global Marketing Business Partner. Against all odds, we beat out larger competitors to win a major $1.8bn CPG deal based on my integrated guerilla marketing campaign strategy and first-of-its-kind cross-functional collaboration.

As an emotionally intelligent leader, I am passionate about fostering a creative, collaborative, and empowering culture. And I am well-versed in leading highly matrixed teams in complex global environments with transparency, clear communication, and a singular vision for success.

projects.title: ISLAMIC BANKING AND FINANCE AND ITS POTENTIAL IN INDIA
projects.description:
Islamic banking is at an incipient stage. The existing legal framework does not permit Islamic Banking. Only selective activities like equity investment is possible, while trade finance aspects like taking title to goods is not possible. A lot of amendments need to be carried out in the prevalent legal set up. Appropriate models need to be selected and implemented to suit society’s diverse financial needs. Islamic Bank of Britain, Islamic banks of Thailand, Singapore and USA may be glaring models for Indian bankers. The reputed domestic and international banks along with the collaboration of RBI should be involved in the process of determining and implementing Islamic Banking products.
The importance and relevance of Islamic banking in India in the context of "Financial Tsunami" that has taken place in recent times further enhances the need of Sharia banking. Also the political parties need economic rationality to convince majority of voters that Islamic banking is not being introduced to please Muslim voters but to genuinely boost faster and inclusive growth for the Indian economy. Obnoxious politics in the name of religion must be avoided. I personally believe to refer ‘Islamic Banking’ as ‘Interest Free Banking’ so that it could be looked through the broad economic kaleidoscope and not a narrow religious prism.

projects.title: SAP – Partner Recruitment, Enablement, and Revenue Generation Project
projects.description:
BACKGROUND: 

Shortlisted by SAP to provide process optimization strategies to reduce revenue turnover cycle from the existing 9 months

PROJECT SUMMARY : 
The overall objective of this project is to provide methods, analysis and recommendations so as to help SAP’s partners achieve faster revenue turnaround times starting from recruitment and going on till revenue generation, especially for Partners in the General Business Segment. This study covers the process type which consists of – Recruitment, Enablement, and Revenue Generation, while also covering the three types of channels – Distributors, VAR, and System Integrators (SI). 

Based on the Partner survey that was conducted by SAP, it revealed important insights into what SAP partners felt about their overall interactions with SAP. The Partners were not satisfied and were least happy with the ease of doing business with SAP in terms of processes, procedures, and the co-operation between sides, the working relationship, and the licencing policies. Based on the feedback received, the partners would like SAP to improve this experience by focusing on improving communication, by enhancing the go-to-market processes and therefore making it easier to do business with SAP. 

To address and solve these issues mentioned, this project leverages and builds on the best practices from other various industries, especially where channel management is a critical process. The industries which have been selected are from– technology, services, banking and fast moving consumer goods. 

The recommendations and solutions have been mapped first by Process which begins from the recruitment of a potential partner to their enablement, then to motivating them to generate revenue and then mapped second, by Channel Partner type to cover the three types of channel partners, namely Value Added Distributor, Value Added Reseller, and System Integrators with my focus and area of project scope being mainly on the System Integrators.

projects.title: Sydney Olympic Park Technical Program - Business Development in APAC
projects.description:
Sydney Olympic Park Authority (SOPA) focuses on managing the transformation of Sydney Olympic Park from a world-class Olympic precinct to a major centre for events, commerce, education and residential development.SOPA’s customized technical programs offer expert insight and professional development to visitors. SOPA has hosted a number of international and domestic visitors namely government & business delegates, professionals, study groups who have benefited from the program.

The program in spite of offering deep insights and professional development was facing a low visitor turn out. A marketing strategy was formulated to address the current challenges, further penetrate the Singapore market and to increase the visitor base. In accordance, we undertook primary & secondary research. The research was done on market diversities & commonalities, business segment analysis (B2B), consumer behavior, product perception, product attributes, new product analysis & usage pattern. The research was conducted through questionnaires, face to face interview, academic and industry literature reviews, whitepapers, case studies, interaction with academic mentors and industry experts. Post the research observations, managerial implications have been highlighted.

Program partners were identified to reach the targeted segments. Program partners were majorly tour and travels agencies and event management companies. A typical sale funnel type approach was followed in the email campaign which consisted of partner identification, contact & follow up with key decision makers and finally collecting the responses as qualified leads. 

To attract and retain key visitors and create a unique experience for them, a tier 5 service framework has been recommended. Personalization and customization of service, harnessing the social media, focusing on the customer relationship management are other recommendations of this report.

about:
Risk Consulting professional with 18 years of experience in risk management, internal audits, enterprise risk management and internal controls review. Proven record of executing enterprise-wide initiatives and enabling data-backed executive decision making.  

Skilled in leading end-to-end project delivery – from risk assessment to high impact reporting. Recognized for cultivating strong client partnerships, business development, building high-performing teams, and embedding a culture of continuous improvement.

experience.description:
Nitin joined Ernst & Young, India as a Director, Risk Consulting – Financial Services sector. 

In this role, Nitin is responsible for managing multiple projects across key client relationships for Financial Services (Banking, NBFCs, Payments’ Aggregators, Insurance and GCC) in Delhi NCR region.

He leads a team of 12-15 highly trained specialists professionals on Internal audits, ITGCs / ITACs, Information Security and other Risk domains. He is responsible for running active business development and GTM initiatives across Service Line solutions including Third Party Risk Management and IT Asset Management services.

experience.position: Associate Director - Internal Audit and Financial Advisory (IAFA)
experience.description:
Nitin was promoted as an Associate Director within the Protiviti Internal Audit practice in January 2023.

In this role, Nitin was responsible for building relationships with clients; and delivering value to clients across the entire host of services including Internal Audit, Enterprise Risk Management, Third Party Risk Management and SOX Compliances.

In this role, Nitin was also responsible for:
• critical KPIs (Utilization, billing, AR, WIP etc.)
• scheduling and utilization of 80+ team members across Partner's cohort
• developing customized solutions and client proposals
• performance development of team of about 20 - 25 internal audits professionals.

experience.position: Senior Manager - Internal Audit and Financial Advisory (IAFA)
experience.description:
Nitin was promoted to Senior Manager, within the internal audit team at Protiviti. His role involved:

• IFC mandate for a large global ITES firm with over 300 controls annually – for 5+ consecutive years (Business and IT Controls).
• ERM Framework for a PE firm owned ‘Green’ energy group of companies – 5 firms.
• TPRM engagements in Managed Business Services (MBS) model involving 20+ professionals for an Indian ITES MNC and a leading Indian Bank.
• Conduct technical training and mentor team members.

experience.position: Manager - Internal Audit and Financial Advisory (IAFA)
experience.description:
Nitin joined internal audit team at Protiviti, Gurgaon in November 2018. He started to work under the leadership of his previous Partner at Genpact, who had also recently joined Protiviti as a Managing Director.

In this role, Nitin led delivery of internal audit mandates across India and Middle Eastern clients of Protiviti. Nitin also spent entire 2019 traveling for large internal audit and controls management projects in Saudi Arabia, Oman and Bahrain.

Starting Dec-2019, Nitin focused entirely on Indian clients across Manufacturing, Technology, Financial Services and Automobile clients. He also led a team of 10-12 professionals across multiple engagements.

Nitin joined a start-up Risk Advisory firm by 2 Ex-EY leaders, that was headquartered in New Delhi, India with substantial operations in Dubai, UAE.

In this role, Nitin was responsible for delivering value to clients across lot of internal audits, clause 49 compliance, review of Standard Operating Procedure for some of the leading clients from Manufacturing, Healthcare and their ancillary companies. 

Nitin also traveled to Angola, Africa for a large-scale project with a UAE headquartered conglomerate; and assisted them with various process and cost efficiency engagements.

In the role of a Manager, Nitin was responsible for coordinating and delivering value to all Axis Risk Consulting (Genpact ERC) clients, in India and globally. 

• Managed and led a team of 5 -7 internal audit professionals on an end-to-end Internal audit engagement for world's largest telecom tower company headquartered in India.
• Led internal controls CoE operations’ team for world’s largest Confectionery brand headquartered in Chicago, US. Responsible to run their Global SOX program and project delivery through 20+ team members.
• Executed an engagement for US’ largest Cranes & Infrastructure Equipment manufacturer, led a Compliance Controllership support engagement across 6 countries. (US, UK & EU, Australia and China

experience.position: Senior - Third Party Risk Management, Risk Consulting
experience.description:
Nitin joined Deloitte USI, Risk Consulting practice under Third Party Risk Management team in Dec-2013.

In this role as a Senior Consultant, Nitin was responsible for delivering value to Fortune 500 clients across Software Asset Management projects for Technology clients. During this period, he executed software licensing engagements and led team of 2-5 professionals.

Nitin joined KPMG Global Services as an Assistant Manager in May 2012 in their Internal Audit practice.

In this role, Nitin was expected to deliver value to the client by collaborating with KPMG U.S in the internal audit and SOX space. Nitin was aligned to serve clients across all sectors with special focus on Financial Services and Technology. 

In this role, Nitin was also responsible for Performance Development of the internal audit team of about 20+ professionals who were aligned under his cohort.

Nitin also travelled onsite to Michigan, US as a co-team member along-with the KPMG US team. During his tenure, he was a KPMG US certified trainer for ‘Advisory Fundamentals for Experienced Hires’ for IARCS team at KPMG Global Services.

experience.position: Lead Assistant Manager - Risk and Financial Management
experience.location: New York, New York, United States
experience.description:
Nitin was promoted in Apr 2011 within EXL's Risk Advisory business and he became a Lead Assistant Manager. 

In this role, Nitin was responsible for managing multiple projects across key client relationships in Europe, South Africa and South-East Asia region, comprising various client locations. He led various SOX, business process improvement and audit engagements across US, Europe, Turkey, Russia and UAE.

In this role, he was leading a team of 7-10 highly trained professionals on Sarbanes Oxley Compliance projects and process improvement projects. In his people management role, he was responsible for coaching and mentoring his team to provide excellent client service. In this role, he was also executing the performance management / development responsibilities for his team.

experience.position: Assistant Manager - Risk and Financial Management
experience.location: New York, New York, United States
experience.description:
In Jan 2009, Nitin was promoted within EXL Risk Advisory practice, and he became an Assistant Manager. In early 2009, Nitin concluded an onsite project in London, UK and did setup an offshore team to transition work to India. From Jun-2009 onwards, Nitin was based out of EXL’s New York, US office and was responsible for assisting the client (a large P&C Insurance company) with their SOX effectiveness evaluation. In this role, Nitin was also responsible for coordinating with EXL's offshore delivery team and setting up a dual shore delivery model. 

Starting end of 2009, Nitin was also assisting in delivering SOX effectiveness engagements across Belgium, France, South Africa, Singapore and Dubai for a world wide evaluation of the client's SOX effectiveness/ readiness. During this time, Nitin had developed deep understanding of client’s business environment; and had experience and knowledge of the client's SOX environment in U.S.

Nitin started off his Corporate Consulting Career with EXL's Risk Advisory practice. Nitin joined EXL as a part of their delivery team in Sep-2006 and executed a business process documentation project for financial business processes of UK’s largest energy company, which was based out of Windsor, England.

Nitin moved to an onsite, client-facing role in Nov-2007 for world’s largest computer hardware company headquartered in Austin, Texas, USA. Thereon, he continued to assist clients across large P&C Insurance companies, along with other fortune 500 companies, onsite based out of United States and United Kingdom.

headline: People Consulting @ EY | Change Management & Workforce Transformation Leader | International Finance, Payroll & HR Operations | Travel SME | Wellness Champion
topSkills: COO • Project Management • Change Management • HR Consulting • Financial Operations
about:
What's your theme in life and work?  For me it's curiosity.  I love learning how things work, how it's built and go behind the scenes.  I ask a lot of questions because I'm genuinely interested to know more.  I'm fascinated by the world and all the moving parts.  

I'm known for solving problems and building without a script. I take that "post it note idea" and turn it into reality.  All done with a sense of humor and a drawer full of chocolate.  My superpowers are being kind, honest and providing high level of customer service to ensure a great experience for all.  

Jack (or Jill) of all trades isn't a bad thing in Operations as it adds a good deal of value to be able to see end to end programs, processes and team evolution.  High level strategy to the day-to-day details is key to being successful in workforce transformation and change programs. 

My ability to pivot, be resilient and navigate the internal politics is just one example of how the diverse projects have shaped me.  I've had opportunities to build, fix and transform organizations which has been so rewarding.  My skills, experience and accomplishments check many boxes across the organization and the titles of the jobs will vary across Private Equity, Financial Services and Management Consulting.  

I keep taking the DISC and other personality tests and no matter how much I try to cheat them; they all agree that my path involves being multi-faceted with diverse skills. 

Competencies:
*Finance | Accounting P&L | Budgets | FP&A
*Business Management - Start Up, Set Up, Private Equity COO
*Director of Operations | Change Management | Business Process 
*HR Operations | HRBP | HR Tax Compliance | Payroll
*Global Business Travel | T&E Policy | Concur T&E | Cross Border Travel Tax & Mobility 
 
Accomplishments 
---Finance & HR transformations, change management and "rock star" short term travel tax (APAC/EMEA) projects
---Forensic payroll accounting audit found $1m in missing P&L items, PTO, vendor overbilling and fraud
---Created a Global Travel Program (T&E) for US & UK Mobility - added duty of care, saved $$, happy travelers
---Created early career talent intern programs to build pipeline and trigger internal mobility

Personal note - 

If you google me, you'll see I help people "travel for less" via my PhilaTravelGirl travel blog and local classes. Travel (50+ countries thus far), international film festivals, F1 and cookies make me happy.  I've met Oprah, hid from hippos in Botswana and been serenaded on Italian tv so I know how to deal with the unexpected adventures in work and life.

experience.position: People Advisory Services - Workforce Transformation Consultant
experience.description:
Trusted leader in People Consulting -Change Management & Transformation in Workforce Advisory.  Working with Fortune 500 clients (sectors include TMT, P/E, Consumer and Financial Services) on global transformation projects which allow me to leverage my Operations experiences in Finance, HR, Payroll, Tax and Mobility to lead workstreams, teams and serve as a SME. 

-HR & Payroll transformations in 20+ countries for TMT and Consumer clients
-M&A carve out to build new processes in HR, Payroll and Finance for new Life Sciences P/E firm
-User lifecycle review for IT and OCM for Consumer client
-Payroll life cycle assessment which included multi-state payroll tax review
-Workforce Management (WFM) Transformation for Consumer client with over 400+ locations and 50k employees

Providing a new perspective on your business at all stages - startup, transformation/turnaround, change management, carve out, M&A and wind down.  
Back office functions - Accounting, Finance, HR, Travel, Facilities, Operations, Tax and DEI.  I wear many hats so you don't have to.  You have the freedom to focus on what you do best.

experience.position: Vice President, HR Operations (Business Travel Mobility Tax Group)
experience.description:
Tax used to be boring but now with Work from Home (WFH), Remote Workforce and Work from Anywhere (WFA) everyone is getting a lesson in state, local and international employee withholding taxes. This project dealt with business travel, mobility and payroll tax compliance. Who knew I was ahead of the curve?  

HR Operations | Global Employer Services | Cross border tax | Multi-state US payroll tax and SALT | Mobility Short Term Travel Tax compliance | WFH and WFA employee and employer withholding tax

Philadelphia & London Operations - MBO backed with private equity funding to form new P/E portfolio company.  AUM $60b+ Institutional, HNW and Family Office clients.

Recruited to build the new U.S. office Finance, HCM, Travel & Operations Corporate Services functions for a private equity financial services portfolio company (International Asset Management & UHNW).  

* Business Unit Controller (US CFO)
* U.S. HR Director Asset Wealth Management
* Global Business Travel Manager (U.S. and London, UK)
* US Office COO/CAO (Chief Administrative Officer - Chief Operations Officer)

Left my corner office for the opportunity to build and create a new office & culture.  My job description was everything NOT Marketing & Client Services or Legal - the rest was fair game! Every day I walked into the office with a schedule and rarely did my day go to plan - that's normal when taking post it note ideas and bringing them to fruition. You need to be comfortable with the unknown - be able to pivot quickly and find creative solutions and deliver an excellent experience for all.

experience.position: AVP, Accounting Manager | Business Travel Manager
experience.description:
Controller's Office Management Accounting Group - Managed General Ledger (G/L), Accounts Payable (Procure to Pay), Travel & Expense (T&E), Fixed Assets and Commisson Accounting functions and teams.  

-Project management, business process mapping, improvement and documentation. Strategy meetings for M&A, new legal entities, outsourcing of business units, closing companies and MBOs. 
-Created centralized Accounts Payable function (20+ legal entities) to manage $180m+ annual spend
-Created Global Business Travel & Expense Management program (Ariba, SAP, Concur) - YOY savings of $100k/year. Negotiated contracts with airlines, hotels, car rental and credit card vendors. 
-DEI with high school and college intern programs. Training programs and job mobility

headline: Senior Manager, Strategy & Transactions at EY
about:
I am a Chicago-based Senior Manager in the Strategy & Transactions practice at EY, performing financial due diligence of transactions across various industries. 

I have 4 years of assurance experience at EY in the financial services industry serving asset management, insurance, and banking and capital markets clients. I have also assisted in IT risk and assurance engagements. I specialized in private equity clients with a portfolio of nonpublic investments with the intention of incorporating finance knowledge in industry audits.

During my career with EY I have developed and executed substantive testing of complex valuation models of mid-market private equity firms specializing in manufacturing and consumer products. This includes the organization of testing design to meet audit objectives and maximize efficiency directly with the client and team executives. I also assess the application of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles in the United States (US GAAP) in financial statement reports and advise improvements involving new reporting requirements.

experience.description:
During this role I have accomplished the following:
	Developed and executed substantive testing of complex valuation models of three mid-market private equity engagements
	Organized testing design and operations audit objectives with client and team executives to maximize efficiency
	Coordinated the efforts of up to three staff members during engagements to achieve audit objectives

During this role I have accomplished the following:
	Conduct various account procedures of integrated financial audits of global insurance providers and broker dealers
	Performed substantive audit procedures over complex valuation models of mid-market private equity firms
	Performed duties as an “Acting Senior” beginning December 2013 on national insurance and private equity engagements

about:
I am a User Experience (UX) Architect and creative design professional specializing in the conceptualization, architecture, design and development of applications, websites, and multimedia interfaces. I possess nearly two decades of industry experience as a user interface (UI) designer, information architect, creative director and front-end web developer.

I regularly mentor and coach a team of UX Architects and UI Designers in the creation of mobile applications and custom web experiences. I am a certified expert in Adobe applications, Sketch, HTML and SASS/CSS.

I closely monitor the UX industry for latest trends and improve upon best practices in UI design and web development. I have a passion for usability, design, and development, and I constantly expand my experience as a leader in the UX community.

experience.description:
I serve as the UX Director and Senior Manager of the Chicago Design Studio at EY. I direct and counsel a team of UX Designers in the creation of mobile applications and custom web experiences. I perform UX consultations and user interviews to assess a client's current business processes and recommend solutions to optimize productivity. Oftentimes, this results in the proposal and implementation of a customized web experience or mobile application to optimize the user's experience. Many of these solutions are integrated with business applications including Microsoft Dynamics, Microsoft Power Apps, and Salesforce platforms.

I am actively engaged in the entire lifecycle of a project from pursuit to delivery. This includes defining the information architecture, mapping screenflows, creating wireframes and interactive prototypes, designing pixel-perfect interfaces, scripting front-end code for implementation, and conducting user testing. As a full-stack designer, I write HTML and SASS/CSS and collaborate with development and QA/UAT teams to ensure the final product's experience aligns with the conceptualized designs.

I served as Director of the UX Architecture team at Sonoma Partners. I mentored and coached a team of UX Architects and Graphic Designers in the creation of mobile applications and custom web experiences. I conducted user interviews and ride-alongs to assess a client's current business processes and recommend solutions to optimize productivity. This often resulted in the proposal and implementation of a customized application or embedded web experience within Microsoft Dynamics or Salesforce platforms to optimize the user's experience and maximize adoption.

I was actively engaged in the entire lifecycle of a project from pursuit to delivery. This included building the information architecture and screenflows, creating wireframes and interactive prototypes, designing pixel-perfect interfaces, and scripting front-end code for implementation. As a full-stack designer, I wrote HTML/CSS and collaborated with the development and QA teams to ensure the final product aligned with the conceptualized designs.

Featured clients include American Airlines, Boston Consulting Group, Cubic Corporation, Merial, and Microsoft.

I served as Creative Director, Information Architect, UX Designer and Web Developer at KeyLimeTie. As Creative Director, I directed the design team in the creation of interactive interfaces for websites, mobile applications, and other touch-devices. As Information Architect, I conceptualized and architected the structure and functionality of all websites and applications. As UX Designer and Web Developer, I designed user interfaces and developed optimized HTML5/CSS3 code to maximize the SEO value and user experience of interactive interfaces.

Additional responsibilities included mentoring and developing the skills of the design team, managing all tasks requested of the creative department, interacting directly with clients to ensure project objectives were completed as requested, providing estimates for RFQs, assigning tasks among the design team to guarantee timely execution of project objectives, maintaining consistent branding standards for all internal and external projects, and managing the organization of all design department materials.

Featured clients include AAA, Allstate, Parts Town, Lava Lamp, Universal Insurance and PLS.

I served as Senior Interactive Designer at Ellison Media Company in the creation of websites, email campaigns, and printed marketing collateral for both internal and external clients. I managed the entire lifecycle of interactive projects including websites and email campaigns from the initial stages of conceptualization and information architecture to the final stages of design, development and implementation. I also created printed and digital advertisements for client products and services, in addition to managing all internal marketing campaigns.

Additionally, I created interactive interfaces for various marketing campaigns and promotional advertisements on websites and emails. I also implemented and supervised the operation of several vehicle decaling programs, and managed the presentation of trade show booth displays.

I owned and operated Scorpio Graphics, a creative services business providing a wide range of services including user interface design, user experience design, information architecture, web development, graphic design, and identity & brand development. headline: Senior Manager, Technology Risk at EY
about:
Chantal is a  Senior Manager in Technology Risk with EY LLP (Ernst & Young LLP) with over sixteen years of client-serving experience in both the Chicago and Phoenix markets. She has more than twelve years of experience in providing IT audit, business internal audit, SSAE18 reporting, and 404 reporting for public and private companies in various industries.  Chantal has two years of experience in the Assurance practice (External Audit), assisting the Firm’s clients in financial statement year-end audits and quarterly reviews for both public and private companies.  She provides value to clients by understanding their risk appetite and exposure, identifying areas of improvement in the internal control framework and providing best practices to strengthen the environment with a US GAAP foundation.

Prior to rejoining EY in 2016, Chantal spent 2 years as a Manager of IT Internal Audit at Hyatt Hotels Corporation in Chicago, IL. Her focus included IT controls, data privacy and information security.  She assisted with leading internal projects focused on IT risk from both a central and property-level perspective.

Chantal is honored to be member of the University of Notre Dame’s Accountancy Advisory Board for the Mendoza College of Business.  With other colleagues and faculty of the University, the Board discusses the future of the Accounting profession, current challenges, and the how to help the University’s students become successful leaders on their professional journey.    Chantal is also a Board Member of the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA), Phoenix Chapter.  With support from the officers and the IIA Board, Chantal is responsible for professional and service-focused activities.

publications.title: EY Human Capital Global Mobility Effectiveness Survey
publications.description: Your talent is in motion — from structured, formal assignments, to ad hoc business travel, to an increasing amount of flexible working arrangements. This range of activity has led to debate over how the mobility function should support the business. Should mobility be integrated with talent management; involved in workforce planning, the business case of the return assignee, identifying and reviewing the return on investment (ROI), proactively managing the risk and cost of the mobility program, tracking the career development and the facilitation of repatriation? Or should the mobility function focus on more operational and administrative tasks for the efficient deployment of the assignee, tracking compliance and the management of all the services required to support the assignment? Or does the role of mobility lie somewhere in between?

projects.title: Jarjarquant
projects.description:
Jarjarquant: A robust approach to quantitative system development

Jarjarquant is a personal project focused on streamlining the early stages of quantitative strategy development. Instead of chasing fully built trading systems, it prioritizes rigorous evaluation of indicators and signals across multiple samples in parallel. The goal is to filter out randomness and overfitting early, making it easier to identify signals with real predictive potential.

Core Features
Purging & Embargoing Data – Prevents look-ahead bias and data leakage.
Multiple Comparisons & Monte Carlo Tests – Ensures signals are statistically meaningful, not just lucky.
Systematic Signal Evaluation – Tests many indicators in parallel while applying strict validation methods.
Why This Project?
Many backtested strategies fail in live markets due to subtle biases. Jarjarquant helps catch these issues early by applying robust statistical safeguards. It’s not about building trading systems—it’s about better understanding which signals actually work and why.

headline: Public Policy & Social Impact Expert |Data Scientist | Government & Business Consulting | Monitoring & Evaluation| Corporate Social Responsibility  | Strategic Management | Big 4 | EY | TISS , MSU Baroda & ISPP Alumni
about:
Manohar is social impact and public policy professional with over a decade of experience driving large-scale development initiatives across livelihoods, governance, and sustainable development. Currently working with EY, he is specialize in designing and implementing evidence-based, outcome-driven programs that strengthen public institutions, improve service delivery, incorporate CRS project into national vision and foster inclusive growth.

Over the years, Manohar has led policy formulation and implementation teams for major development initiatives in collaboration with various state government departments and Corporate (CSR project) including the Chief Minister’s Office of Rajasthan and the Finance Department. His notable projects include the Chief Minister Service deliver cell, Rajasthan Agriculture Competitiveness Project (RACP), Swachh Bharat Mission, National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM), and poverty mitigation programs in Western Rajasthan. These projects were supported by a range of donors, including the World Bank, Government of India, Government of Rajasthan, Tata Trusts, and IFAID.

He has extensive experience working across both publicly and privately funded programs, often operating at the intersection of governance reform, policy innovation, and social entrepreneurship. My approach combines analytical rigor with community-centric perspectives—ensuring that interventions are not only data-driven but also equitable and sustainable.
Academically he holds a Master’s degree in Social Work from the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS), a Post Graduate Program in Public Policy, Design and Management from the Indian School of Public Policy (ISPP), and an MA in Economics from The Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda. Additionally, he has completed certificate programs from the University of Chicago and the "Anubhav Lecture Series" at the UChicago Delhi Center.
He is passionate about leveraging public policy, innovation, and collaborative governance to create systems that enable people and communities to thrive. he is always open to conversations around policy consulting, social impact strategy, governance transformation, and sustainable development partnerships.

headline: Healthcare Attorney | JD, CHC, 340B ACE
about:
Healthcare regulatory attorney and consultant with focused experience advising life sciences companies and healthcare entities on complex federal and state regulatory matters, including drug pricing, fraud and abuse, and government reimbursement programs. 

My work centers on 340B, the Medicaid Drug Rebate Program, and Medicare-related compliance, with experience translating evolving regulatory guidance, litigation risk, and policy changes into practical, defensible strategies.

I bring a hands-on, on-the-ground perspective, having worked directly with hospitals, pharmaceutical companies, and compliance teams to assess operational risk, support internal reviews, and advise on real-world implementation of regulatory requirements. In consulting, I have led whiteboard sessions and executive-level discussions on the implications of ongoing litigation and industry-wide regulatory developments, and have served as a keynote speaker at healthcare conferences, presenting on emerging trends in healthcare regulation and compliance.

I am particularly drawn to high-profile counseling, investigations, and interdisciplinary work, and value environments that emphasize rigorous analysis, strong writing, mentorship, and collaboration across regulatory, litigation, and transactional teams.

Outside of my professional work, I stay grounded through long-distance running, classical Indian dance, and Carnatic music, which reinforce the discipline and creativity I bring to my practice.

Always open to thoughtful collaboration and growth. Let’s connect.

This campaign was the second we created that helped drive record-breaking sales.

From C-Suite executives to product engineers, I love rolling up my sleeves to craft narratives, train people for stepping on the stage or in front of the camera, and reach new audiences with their story.  I am particularly honored to have been a part of the team who helped Satya Nadella tell his personal story through his 2017 book “Hit Refresh” for which I managed Satya’s global television appearances.

Partner at EY Consulting - AI & Data Leader for EY New Zealand
about:
I'm an EY Consulting Partner based in Auckland and have spent my career in consulting and industry leadership roles enabling telecommunications, financial services and public service organisations to deliver noticeably better outcomes for their customers, staff and shareholders.

I work with our client leaders and their teams to shape practical strategies and drive speed to value through lean agile deliveries.  

As AI adoption builds momentum, I am working to help client leaders and their teams to understand where how to make AI a successful member of their front-line teams.

experience.description: Since 2011 I have been working with our public and private sector clients in New Zealand to shape and drive transformation.  Our goal is to help our clients to leverage the best of EY global experience in ways that work in our New Zealand context.

I worked with Westpac New Zealand in various senior operational and change leadership roles from 2005 to 2011.

Initially, I worked with the executive team over 18 months to define and manage strategy and processes to redirect investment to a portfolio of change more biased towards customer experience and revenue driving investments.

Next, I led the credit card & merchant operations business unit.  In this  role I led a team to implement quantitative methods for management and delivered over 25% cost reduction in year 1, improved staff engagement, improved customer delivery and improved operational risk profile.  In parallel to this I established the national Operations Development Team to drive sustainable delivery performance improvement across all back office functions. 

Following my operations role, I moved into front-line retail network leadership for Auckland Metro.  In this role I led our retail distribution teams in Auckland city.   I led our retail teams through the first phases of the GFC (an intense time for our business, our staff and our customers) during which we successfully grew and self funded our balance sheet, grew customer numbers and improved customer net promoter scores.

My final role with Westpac was Retail Banking Simplification Leader.  In this role I lead a PI team of working with  stakeholders to improve transaction banking and lending performance across our national retail network.  We used a combination of methods to systematically identify improvement opportunities, deliver and embed change. During this time the team dramatically simplified branch banking, cash management and lending.  The high-point of this role was reduction of median loan approval time from 3 days to 40 minutes and our bank moving from market trailing to market leading for customer experience and market share.

Through my time at Westpac I was a member of the senior team defining bank strategy and participating in other leadership initiatives.

During my time with The Berkeley Partnership I worked with as Programme Director for a global  transformation programme for the trading arm of a global energy company.  In this role I was responsible for delivery strategy, senior stakeholder engagement and delivery team leadership.  We ran this project across Singapore, London, Chicago and Houston.

Over my seven years with Accenture I worked with various energy, financial services and telecommunications clients in the UK and Ireland.  

Initially, I worked with a large UK energy company as part of a team delivering core billing and CRM systems preparing them to compete in a deregulated energy market.

Next, I worked with The London Stock exchange as technical lead on a programme to replace the Regulatory News Service, the channel all listed companies must use for all company disclosures.

Following the LSE, I moved to Ireland and spend two years working with Eircom, the Irish national Telco.  For the first year, I led a team to deliver Siebel CRM capability to a newly formed SME business unit.  During my second year at Eircom I worked with their senior team to create a new broadband business. 

During my final few years with Accenture I delivered a number of projects at British Telecom.  Firstly I worked with their Retail Sales & Service team implementing Siebel CRM and their first multi-channel contact centre.  My last role at BT was leading the Customer Provisioning Transformation programme at BT wholesale as part of BT retail/wholesale separation preparations.  In this role I led a large multi-supplier team to define strategy, to plan and to build a provisioning capability to serve new retail market players.

During my time with Accenture I established our multi-channel contact centre of excellence in London which was subsequently used as a key asset for our large scale contact centre off shoring programmes.

headline: Americas International Tax and Transaction Services Director of Strategic Operations at EY
about:
I have over 25 years of experience in public accounting and have focused the past 12+ years as the director of strategy and operations for the International Tax and Transaction Services (ITTS) practice and, prior to that, the Transaction Tax (TT) practice. In these roles, I wear many hats, primarily focusing on strategizing, developing and executing on our business plan, strategic priorities and other operational matters, including talent matters, diversity and inclusion, markets, finance, technology, and change management (e.g., integrating two practices (international tax and transaction tax practices), developing and implementing our apprenticeship model, and moving from a Region to National model). I have led efforts in developing a framework for our SharePoint sites, creating various leadership videos, budgeting, drafting communications, facilitating and managing various meetings, developing collateral/thought leadership, reviewing data metrics to spot trends, organizing and coordinating learning and development matters, etc. Throughout each of these efforts, I have exhibited strong project management and leadership skills. Prior to these roles, I spent 7 years in client service specializing in advising private equity and corporate clients on numerous tax aspects of mergers and acquisitions and 5 years at another public accounting firm. 

I hold a bachelor’s of science degree in Accounting from the University of Kentucky and a Juris Doctorate and LL.M. In Taxation from The University of Illinois Chicago School of Law. I am a licensed attorney in the State of Illinois. I am also a member of the American Bar Association, Illinois State Bar Association and Chicago Bar Association.

Our Client (one of the leading companies in CPG industry in the US) currently is unable to take into account of external data into their forecasting mode. In the era of BIG DATA, out client is eager to know how BIG DATA Analytic is able to sense the short-term demand change in order to adjust sales forecast. 

Firstly, my team did comprehensive research on Consumer Behaivour Principle, Literature Review and consulted domain experts to determine what are relevant factors that may affect the sales of the particular product. 

Secondly, we collected data from various sources, both structured and unstructured. We cleaned up all data and tested them in statistical model to approve/disapprove our hypotheses. 

Thirdly,  we iteratively analyzed and modified model to deliver most valuable business insights. 

Outcomes: 
1. Our model achieved 90%+ explanatory power of historical sales data.
2. Our forecast model increased forecast accuracy by 11% compared to original forecast
3. Insights on how different regions respond differently to various events
4. Scalable model for our customer to apply on other products

experience.position: Manager, Tax Accounting and Risk Advisory Services (TARAS)
experience.description:
As a Manager at EY, I lead teams in delivering complex tax accounting and compliance solutions for multinational corporations and high-growth businesses. I specialize in ASC 740 income tax accounting, overseeing the preparation and review of tax provisions, deferred tax analysis, and management of uncertain tax positions to ensure accurate and transparent financial reporting under U.S. GAAP.

I advise clients on significant transactions, including spin-offs, carve-outs, mergers, and acquisitions, providing technical guidance on tax implications and ensuring proper recognition and disclosure in financial statements. I drive process improvements by leveraging technology and best practices to streamline tax provision workflows, reduce cycle times, and strengthen governance.

In addition to client service, I manage and mentor high-performing teams, fostering collaboration and professional development. Through strategic leadership and proactive communication, I deliver insights that help clients mitigate risk, optimize tax strategies, and create long-term value.

As a Senior Tax Associate at EY, I specialized in ASC 740 income tax accounting and supported clients through complex tax reporting and compliance challenges. I prepared and reviewed tax provisions, performed deferred tax analysis, and managed uncertain tax positions to ensure accurate financial reporting under U.S. GAAP. My work included advising on the tax implications of significant transactions such as spin-offs, carve-outs, mergers, and acquisitions, ensuring proper recognition and disclosure in financial statements.

I collaborated with cross-functional teams to analyze the impact of tax law changes and transactional structures on income tax accounting. I implemented process improvements and leveraged technology to streamline tax provision workflows, reduce cycle times, and enhance governance. By providing technical guidance and actionable insights, I helped clients mitigate risk, optimize tax strategies, and maintain transparency for stakeholders. Through proactive communication and a commitment to excellence, I built strong relationships and contributed to projects that drove compliance and created long-term value.

As a seasoned tax professional with extensive experience in accounting for income taxes under ASC 740, I have had the privilege of working with Deloitte's ASC740 group and the National Tax Accounting Group (NTAG). In this role, I have helped clients navigate the complexities of tax accounting, providing technical guidance and support on a wide range of tax-related financial reporting matters.

Working with clients across various industries and sectors, I have leveraged my deep understanding of ASC 740 to help ensure compliance with financial reporting requirements while minimizing tax liabilities. My expertise in accounting for uncertain tax positions, tax provision preparation and review, and tax compliance support has enabled me to provide clients with actionable insights and recommendations that drive business success.

Through my experience with the ASC740 group and NTAG, I have honed my skills in tax accounting and financial reporting, developing a keen eye for detail and a deep appreciation for the importance of accuracy and precision in this field. I am committed to providing my clients with best-in-class service, and I am constantly seeking new ways to improve my expertise and stay at the forefront of the latest industry trends.

As a Tax Intern in Deloitte’s National Tax Accounting Group, I specialized in supporting ASC 740-focused tax advisory and risk management services for a diverse portfolio of clients. My role involved assisting multidisciplinary teams in addressing complex tax accounting challenges under ASC 740, contributing to solutions that enhanced financial reporting accuracy and mitigated risk.

Key Responsibilities:

- Assisted in conducting ASC 740 research and analysis to support tax provision optimization, management of uncertain tax positions, and assessment of deferred tax assets and liabilities. Contributed to improving provision accuracy through detailed analysis and data validation.

- Supported the design and implementation of ASC 740-compliant tax provision processes for global organizations, ensuring alignment with GAAP standards. Helped develop frameworks that contributed to reducing quarterly provision variances.

- Assisted in analyzing the ASC 740 implications of evolving tax legislation, such as global tax reforms and digital taxation trends, and supported the development of proactive strategies to maintain financial reporting integrity. Participated in a project to integrate new tax rules into client provision models.

- Supported the team in collaborating with clients to understand their business needs and align ASC 740 strategies with their financial objectives, contributing to the delivery of customized solutions.

- Participated in training sessions and workshops to deepen understanding of ASC 740 and tax accounting principles, enhancing ability to contribute effectively to client engagements.

headline: Global Treasurer
about:
As EY’s Americas Administration Leader, I lead our US firm’s Investment and Treasury operations, as well as our Administrative and Workplace Services functions. I am a member of the Board of Directors for EY’s captive insurance company and EY Global Finance and I serve as the Chairman of the US firm’s Retirement Investment Committee.

Most recently, I was named to EY Americas Environmental, Social and Governance leadership team as the US Corporate Sustainability Leader, where I help drive EY’s continued commitment to becoming a more sustainable organization. 

Prior to my current roles, I spent the majority of my career in EY’s Strategy & Transactions practice (formerly Transaction Advisory Services), where I served as the Americas TAS Quality and Risk Management Leader. During my more than 30 years’ experience, I have successfully delivered transaction-related services to a variety of companies, including corporate and private equity clients. 

As a long-time advocate for disability inclusion, I serve on the Board of Directors for Disability:IN, a national non-profit committed to expanding opportunities in the workplace for people with disabilities. For the past eight years, I have served as the Executive Sponsor of EY’s AccessAbilities professional network. 

I’m also on the Board of Trustees for Ursuline Academy, a private college preparatory school dedicated to educating and inspiring young women to learn and lead.

about:
Hello there! Thanks for viewing my profile. I’m a cybersecurity and risk management professional with 7+ years of experience advising Fortune 500 companies across healthcare, finance, and technology sectors. With certifications including CISSP, CPA, CISA, and Azure AI Fundamentals, I specialize in building scalable, metrics-driven compliance programs that support business growth and regulatory resilience.

My expertise spans across HITRUST, NIST CSF, GDPR, HIPAA, and third-party risk, with a strong track record of leading cross-functional teams, delivering strategic assessments, and driving measurable impact. 

I also support client acquisition through proposal development and go-to-market enablement, and mentor future leaders to build sustainable team success.

Let’s connect if you're looking to drive enterprise security strategy, improve regulatory posture, or grow your GRC program with a trusted advisor.

publications.title: An Underserved Population: Rural Mental Health Needs in West Texas
publications.description:
The purpose of the research was to obtain quantifiable data about the mental health needs and availability of counseling services in rural communities surrounding Abilene, Texas. A survey with socio-demographic questions and enquiries on the mental health needs in the community was created. This survey was then distributed via e-mail to relevant people and institutions in several counties surrounding Abilene (Taylor County), such as those within the Region 14 education system - school counselors, school administrators, community leaders, local law enforcement, firefighters, clinics, and churches. 127 responses were received in total.

This research revealed the need for more quality mental health services in rural communities, specifically telemental health services. Subsequently, this study provided insight for students and professors in the HSU psychology and counseling graduate program on their plans to begin an online video-conferencing counseling service in the Hardin-Simmons University Counseling Center.

This study's findings were presented orally at the Texas Tech University Undergraduate Research Conference on March 29 and at Abilene Christian University Undergraduate Research Conference on April 5.

experience.description:
The MINDEF is a ministry of the Government of Singapore entrusted with overseeing the national defence needs of the Republic of Singapore.

As an Assistant Director, I am responsible for directing the development and execution of the Ministry of Defence’s international engagement in the strategic communications domain, such as international organisations, government, and think-tanks to promote international collaborations and affiliations. I also manage 3 direct reports and 6 global portfolio managers.

I directed the development of a strategic communications international engagement framework. This framework informed the current and future engagements with strategic communications international partners for the next 2 to 3 years. I also created briefs and strategic communications-related input for Ministerial and senior management-level international engagements with defence partners worldwide. Through these efforts, nascent strategic communications ties with defence partners have been established, and the organisation’s day-to-day operations have become more efficient.

In this role, I was responsible for leading the planning and development of strategic communications efforts to support and maintain public trust in National Service, the Ministry of Defence, and the Singapore Armed Forces. 

Leveraging my in-depth understanding of legislation, I headed the review of 3 complex pieces of legislations. I subsequently led the implementation of one of the pieces of new legislation, which involved instituting expected internal work processes, timelines, and frameworks. I also spearheaded strategic communications plans for 3 campaigns and proposed initiatives and messages to sustain organisation-wide efforts.

During this time, I was responsible for managing the evaluation and development of the Ministry of Defence and the Singapore Armed Forces’ personnel development policies, including performance management, ranking and promotion, and career transition and secondment to ensure a fair and unbiased system.

I led the review, development, and execution of the organisation’s revised performance management system. I also supported the development and implementation of a framework for civilian personnel competencies, standardising personnel assessment. By managing daily cases and queries from personnel management centres, I obtained first-hand information on the policy’s direct impact that enabled me to determine policy effectiveness.

Having served as a Defence Policy Officer, I was responsible for formulating defence relations policies and strategies to shape and advance Singapore’s defence relations interests with Southeast Asian and European countries. Reported to the Assistant Director (Defence Policy).

I participated in various global conferences and country-to-country dialogues. This required managing trip briefs, crystallising defence relations interests with relevant countries, and collating input from different stakeholders. I also facilitated meetings between senior management and foreign dignitaries at multilateral events. Collaborating with internal agencies and the Legal Services department, I managed various pieces of legislation, such as Defence Cooperation Agreements. These efforts played a pivotal role in solidifying defence relationships with key partners and establishing Singapore as the security cooperation partner of choice in the region.

publications.title: Article 12ad of the Dutch Corporate Income Tax Act 1969: a mismatch compared to the EU ATAD2-Directive?
publications.description: Original Dutch title: Art. 12ad Wet VPB 1969: een mismatch ten opzichte van de ATAD2-Richtlijn?

publications.title: Asymmetry as a result of the concurrence between the anti-mismatch rules and the interest deduction limitations because of the broad concept of a deduction
publications.description:
In this article, I argue that because of the broad concept of a deduction pursuant to the anti-(hybrid) mismatch rules, the outcome of the application of each of these anti-(hybrid) mismatch rules is different if, either at the level of the taxpayer (if it is the debtor) or at the level of the (related) debtor (if the taxpayer is the creditor), interest deduction limitations apply.

This asymmetric outcome is not in line with the EU’s ATAD2 Directive and results in both an overkill as well as an underkill in certain situations. In my article I therefore recommend that it would be better to align the Dutch ATAD2 rules with the rules pursuant to the EU’s ATAD2 Directive, as this would resolve most of the issues.

publications.title: Hybridemismatches involving a permanent establishment in light of the origin requirement of the Dutch ATAD2 rules
publications.description: Original (Dutch) title: Hybridemismatches met een vaste inrichting in het licht van de oorsprongseis van ATAD2

publications.title: Secondary transactions and the Bill to counteract mismatches involving the arm’s length principle
publications.description: I analyze the application of the Bill to counteract mismatches involving the arm’s length principle (Wet tegengaan mismatches bij toepassing zakelijkheidsbeginsel) with respect to the “informal capital-doctrine” created by the Dutch Supreme Court. Further to providing an overview of the rules applicable, I argue that the Bill is not applicable to indirect secondary transactions (i.e., non-arm’s length transfers not involving a Dutch taxpayer) and that there are good argument to conclude participation exemption should be applicable with respect to gains embedded as a result of non-arm’s length transfers countered by this Bill. Finally, I analyze the circumstances under which capital transactions are affected by the Bill.

publications.title: The beneficiary pursuant to the Withholding Tax Act 2021
publications.description:
In this article, I analyze the definition of the beneficiary pursuant to the Withholding Tax Act 2021. I analyze amongst others which entity qualifies as the beneficiary for Dutch withholding tax purposes in case of a split of the economic and legal title of the ownership to interest/royalty payments, the qualification of a (quasi)hybrid entity for withholding tax purposes and which entity as the beneficiary in case of such a (quasi)hybrid entity.

Furthermore, I analyze which entity qualifies as the beneficiary in case of a (third-party) loan provided under a guarantee from a related party. In such instances, the guarantor should in principle qualify as the beneficiary, but it could also be argued that in case of third-party debt in such instances no withholding tax should be due.

As a Technology Consulting Manager at EY, I lead the development of product and data solutions that help financial institutions operate with greater speed, accuracy, and control. My work bridges product strategy, data engineering, and operations.

Over the past several years, I’ve helped design and deliver end-to-end platforms for risk and finance transformation, including Credit Risk frameworks that automate end to end financial reporting, improve transparency, and strengthen governance and controls.

I’m deeply experienced in product management, data analytics, and stakeholder management, guiding cross-functional teams through every phase of delivery from defining requirements to full-scale implementation. My daily technical stack includes Python, SQL, and Power BI, which I use to manipulate data and actionable visualizations for executive decision-making.

volunteering.description: As a Chicago Scholars mentor, I am paired with Scholars from across the Chicagoland area for two years to serve as an important guide and offer advice to first-generation and under-resourced youth throughout the college admissions process, the transition to college, and their first year of college classes.

In the US, up to 65% of jobs require post-secondary education, but too many underserved high school students don’t consider going to college. The goal can seem too distant, the application process too confusing, the cost too expensive and the rewards too unclear.

EY College MAP addresses this gap by matching employee volunteer mentors with groups of 11th- and 12th-graders in underserved high schools throughout the US so that they can gain access to college and succeed in higher education. The program helps demystify the process of applying to and affording college, encouraging students who might not otherwise have considered it an option. We then work with students to build the skills and the confidence they need to persist in completing their post-secondary goals

Issues addressed in fraud investigations include inappropriate revenue recognition and earnings manipulation, as well as embezzlement, occupational abuse, and vendor kick-back schemes. Chris has coordinated Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and False Claims Act investigations.  He regularly assists clients with transaction forensics services, including assessing fraud and corruption risks in cross-border acquisitions.  

During the COVID-19 pandemic, Chris has helped clients with disaster recovery and federal relief programs.  Past and current projects relate to maximizing financial recovery from government and commercial insurance.  These projects have centered around recovery from the CARES Act, Coronavirus Relief Act, FEMA and the American Rescue Plan (Fiscal Recovery Fund).  He has experience with interacting with federal government agencies and has guided clients on federal program compliance requirements, including Uniform Guidance / 2 CFR 200.
Chris was a Senior Manager in Ernst & Young’s Forensic and Integrity Services practice. His focus was on fraud investigations and anti-corruption investigations.

Chris was a Senior Manager in the Assurance Services practice of Ernst & Young in Chicago, IL.  He provided audit and assurance services to public and privately-held companies in the life sciences, retail, manufacturing, airline and construction industries. Chris was responsible for evaluating client accounting and reporting methodologies to ensure that financial reports are prepared in accordance with SEC rules and regulations and U.S. generally accepted accounting principles. 

He was previously on secondment with Ernst & Young AG in Munich, Germany.  During that time, Chris served large subsidiaries of US parent companies, as well as domestic German companies in need of US GAAP and SEC reporting expertise.

about:
Specialized in the area of Investment Management and Real Estate.

experience.description:
Senior tax manager in Ernst & Young’s West Sub-Area Indirect and State & Local Tax (“SALT”) Practice based in Irvine, California, with over 20 years of tax expertise serving a variety of industries. Specializing in multi-state income/franchise taxes as well as state and federal business credits and incentives.
 
Significant experience with federal and multi-state issues of pass through entities, including RICs, partnerships and REITs. Including but not limited to state and federal tax credits, enterprise and empowerment zone programs, and related tax planning.
Specializing in taxation of the investment management industry.
Served middle market clients in the private company services group.
Audit and tax intern for construction / real estate group.
